# iwe bare front matter support

## Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some wiki systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top of the file, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

## Design

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: `
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

If the first line is not `title: `, no bare front matter is detected; the file is parsed normally.

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives (e.g., prose starting with `Something: explanation`). No key whitelist is needed — `title` as a mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely over time.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false` (current behavior preserved).

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (or the events reader), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, detect bare headers per the rule above
- Wrap the detected block with `---` delimiters so pulldown_cmark parses it as a metadata block
- The rest of the pipeline (metadata storage, title extraction, graph) works unchanged

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled:
- Emit metadata as bare `key: value` lines followed by a blank line — no `---` fences
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand YAML front matter delimiters

### Scope of changes

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs` — add `bare_frontmatter` field
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` or `crates/liwe/src/markdown/reader.rs` — pre-process content
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs` — conditional fence suppression
- Tests for: detection, round-trip, no false positive on prose, interaction with `---` fenced files

## Future: metadata querying

Once front matter is reliably parsed (bare or fenced), add `--meta key=value` filtering to `iwe find`. This enables task tracking via front matter fields like `status: active`, `depends: concurrency-design`, etc., queryable from the CLI.

## Compatibility note

TibbitWiki uses four keys: `title`, `tags`, `created`, `modified`. Enabling `bare_frontmatter` in an iwe workspace pointing at wiki notes would let iwe read them natively. The writer would emit bare headers, preserving compatibility with the wiki.

# iwe bare front matter support

## Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some wiki systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top of the file, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

## Design

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: `
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

If the first line is not `title: `, no bare front matter is detected; the file is parsed normally.

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives (e.g., prose starting with `Something: explanation`). No key whitelist is needed — `title` as a mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely over time.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false` (current behavior preserved).

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (or the events reader), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, detect bare headers per the rule above
- Wrap the detected block with `---` delimiters so pulldown_cmark parses it as a metadata block
- The rest of the pipeline (metadata storage, title extraction, graph) works unchanged

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled:
- Emit metadata as bare `key: value` lines followed by a blank line — no `---` fences
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand YAML front matter delimiters

### Scope of changes

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs` — add `bare_frontmatter` field
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` or `crates/liwe/src/markdown/reader.rs` — pre-process content
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs` — conditional fence suppression
- Tests for: detection, round-trip, no false positive on prose, interaction with `---` fenced files

## Future: metadata querying

Once front matter is reliably parsed (bare or fenced), add `--meta key=value` filtering to `iwe find`. This enables task tracking via front matter fields like `status: active`, `depends: concurrency-design`, etc., queryable from the CLI.

## Compatibility note

TibbitWiki uses four keys: `title`, `tags`, `created`, `modified`. Enabling `bare_frontmatter` in an iwe workspace pointing at wiki notes would let iwe read them natively. The writer would emit bare headers, preserving compatibility with the wiki.
---

Found the bug. In `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`, `wrap_bare_frontmatter` filters out lines starting with a space when building `cleaned_header`. That strips indented YAML continuations like list items:

```
depends:
  - foo
```

The `  - foo` line is removed, leaving `depends:` with no value, so `--meta depends=foo` never matches. Fenced front matter bypasses this code path entirely, which is why it works there.

The filter has no real purpose — the blank line already terminates the header block. Let me remove it and add a regression test.

content.thinking: I'm realizing the tests don't cover sequence values in bare frontmatter, and I've found the bug: the `cleaned_header` filter in `wrap_bare_frontmatter` is stripping out indented YAML lines like list items because it removes anything starting with a space. The filter is too broad — it was probably meant to keep body content out, but since blank lines already separate frontmatter from the body, this aggressive filtering shouldn't be necessary.

content.text:
Found the bug. In `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`, `wrap_bare_frontmatter` filters out lines starting with a space when building `cleaned_header`. That strips indented YAML continuations like list items:

```
depends:
  - foo
```

The `  - foo` line is removed, leaving `depends:` with no value, so `--meta depends=foo` never matches. Fenced front matter bypasses this code path entirely, which is why it works there.

The filter has no real purpose — the blank line already terminates the header block. Let me remove it and add a regression test.

content.text:
# iwe bare front matter support

## Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some wiki systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top of the file, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

## Design

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: `
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

If the first line is not `title: `, no bare front matter is detected; the file is parsed normally.

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives (e.g., prose starting with `Something: explanation`). No key whitelist is needed — `title` as a mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely over time.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false` (current behavior preserved).

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (or the events reader), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, detect bare headers per the rule above
- Wrap the detected block with `---` delimiters so pulldown_cmark parses it as a metadata block
- The rest of the pipeline (metadata storage, title extraction, graph) works unchanged

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled:
- Emit metadata as bare `key: value` lines followed by a blank line — no `---` fences
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand YAML front matter delimiters

### Scope of changes

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs` — add `bare_frontmatter` field
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` or `crates/liwe/src/markdown/reader.rs` — pre-process content
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs` — conditional fence suppression
- Tests for: detection, round-trip, no false positive on prose, interaction with `---` fenced files

## Future: metadata querying

Once front matter is reliably parsed (bare or fenced), add `--meta key=value` filtering to `iwe find`. This enables task tracking via front matter fields like `status: active`, `depends: concurrency-design`, etc., queryable from the CLI.

## Compatibility note

TibbitWiki uses four keys: `title`, `tags`, `created`, `modified`. Enabling `bare_frontmatter` in an iwe workspace pointing at wiki notes would let iwe read them natively. The writer would emit bare headers, preserving compatibility with the wiki.

I'm realizing the issue with the `cleaned_header` filter — it strips out indented lines, but YAML list items under `depends:` are typically indented with spaces before the dash, so those lines get removed entirely. This means if a user has a standard YAML structure with indented list items, the filter would be eliminating the actual dependency data.

I'm realizing the tests don't cover sequence values in bare frontmatter, and I've found the bug: the `cleaned_header` filter in `wrap_bare_frontmatter` is stripping out indented YAML lines like list items because it removes anything starting with a space. The filter is too broad — it was probably meant to keep body content out, but since blank lines already separate frontmatter from the body, this aggressive filtering shouldn't be necessary.

content.text:
Found the bug. In `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`, `wrap_bare_frontmatter` filters out lines starting with a space when building `cleaned_header`. That strips indented YAML continuations like list items:

```
depends:
  - foo
```

The `  - foo` line is removed, leaving `depends:` with no value, so `--meta depends=foo` never matches. Fenced front matter bypasses this code path entirely, which is why it works there.

The filter has no real purpose — the blank line already terminates the header block. Let me remove it and add a regression test.

## Summary

**Bug:** In `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`, `wrap_bare_frontmatter` filtered out every line starting with a space when wrapping the bare header in `---` fences:

```rust
header.lines().filter(|l| !l.starts_with(' '))
```

For YAML mappings whose value is a sequence:

```
title: Foo
depends:
  - foo
```

the indented `  - foo` line was stripped, so the wrapped block became `depends:` with no value. Metadata was parsed as `depends: ~`, and `--meta depends=foo` could never match. Fenced (`---`) front matter goes straight to pulldown-cmark and bypasses this code, so it kept working — and no existing test exercised list-valued bare front matter, so all tests still passed.

**Fix:** Removed the `starts_with(' ')` filter — the blank line already terminates the header block, so indented YAML continuation lines should be preserved verbatim. Added regression test `bare_frontmatter_preserves_yaml_sequence_values` that imports a bare header with a `depends:` sequence and asserts the parsed YAML contains both list items. `cargo test` is fully green.
